;Business and economy
*[[Artificial intelligence arms race]]
**[[Google]] reports that they will not renew a contract with the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] to develop [[machine learning]] algorithms for [[military drone|drones]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44341490 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2018 lower Puna eruption]]
**More than 80 homes have now been destroyed by the Kilauea eruption. [http://ktla.com/2018/06/02/more-than-80-homes-have-been-destroyed-by-kilauea-volcano-eruption-in-hawaii/ (KTLA)] 
**Lava from [[Kīlauea]] boils [[Hawaii]]'s [[Green Lake (Hawaii)|Green Lake]] and spills across numerous highways. [https://www.npr.org/2018/06/07/617860832/lava-from-kilauea-boils-away-freshwater-lake-in-hawaii (NPR)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**The funeral of a 21-year-old medic, Razan al-Najjar, draws thousands of [[Palestinians]]. Witnesses say that Razan was killed while trying to evacuate a wounded protester lying on the [[Israel]]i side of the fence. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2018/06/02/Thousands-mourn-Palestinian-medic-killed-by-Israeli-gunfire/1541527984313/ (UPI)]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of the Philippines]]
**Shortly before leaving for [[South Korea]], the [[President of the Philippines]], [[Rodrigo Duterte]], tells the [[United Nations]] Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers [[Diego García Sayán]] that "he can go to hell". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-duterte-un/philippines-duterte-tells-u-n-human-rights-expert-go-to-hell-idUSKCN1IZ063 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The new [[Torra Government|Catalan regional government]] takes office in [[Barcelona]]. The 7-month-long application of Article 155 of the [[Constitution of Spain|Spanish Constitution]] is thus lifted, meaning that [[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis#Independence declaration and direct rule|direct rule]] is over. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/spain-ceases-direct-rule-in-catalonia-1527941307 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[2018 vote of no confidence in the government of Mariano Rajoy]]
**[[Pedro Sánchez]], a member of the [[Spanish Socialist Party]], is sworn in as [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] before King [[Felipe VI]]. Sánchez opts to take the oath without a [[bible]] or [[crucifix]]; a first in modern [[History of Spain|Spanish history]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44340879 (BBC)]
*Thousands protest in [[Amman]] and other [[Jordan]]ian cities, despite King [[Abdullah II of Jordan|Abdullah II]] ordering a freeze on controversial fuel and electricity price increases. [http://www.middleeasteye.net/news/jordan-protests-continue-despite-price-rise-freeze-1202269757 (''Middle East Eye'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/jun/03/jordan-amman-protest-imf-austerity-measures (''The Guardian'')]
